3. Sheikh Liakat Ali and two others tiled Writ Petition No.333 of 1993 in the High Court Division challenging the orders passed in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 and taking over possession of the land and the structure of holding No.14/1, Topkhana Road, Dhaka stating that they are the owners of the "Usree" house and the land measuring an area of .4925 acre of khas mohal plot No. 188, ward No.3, Sheet No.20, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as "disputed property"). The disputed property originally belonged to the Collectorate of Dhaka who settled the same to Satyendra Nath Roy (S.N.Roy), Professor of the University of Dhaka on 08.12.1937 for a period of 23 years 3 months by a registered deed of lease. Satyendra Nath Roy constructed two storied building thereon and named the same as "Usree". He gifted the disputed property to his wife Sreemoti Sujata Roy by registered deed dated 18.05.1940. The Government requisitioned the said building on 23.09.1947 and paid rent to Sujata Roy. Sujata Roy transferred the said property to Munshi Ashraf Ali, predecessor-in-interest of the writ petitioner-respondents by a registered sale deed dated 26.03.1951. Said Ashraf Ali got the order of lease extended by registered deed of lease dated 07.08.1961. Ashraf Ali submitted several representations to the Government to get the said property released from the order of requisition. Thus, the Government de-requisitioned the said "Usree" house on 09.07.1971. He let out the said house to Bangladesh National Awami Party (NAP). After creation of BAKSAL in January 1975, NAP was merged with BAKSAL. NAP left the disputed house in May 1975. Ashraf Ali went to ascertain the position of the disputed property and found that the police locked up the house and posted police force for its security. On inquiry, he came to know that the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka had taken over possession of the said house. Ashraf Ali went to the office of the Deputy Commissioner and he was informed that the disputed property had been acquired by the Government in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 for construction of the building of Press Club. No notice for acquisition was ever served upon Ashraf Ali. He submitted several representations to the Government to get the said property released from acquisition. Ashraf All died on 18.03.1976 and his wife died on 05.04.1992. Thereafter, his heirs the petitioners made similar representations that notice of acquisition was served upon the owner of the disputed property and that the building of the Press Club was constructed elsewhere so they are entitled to get the disputed property released. Meanwhile, the possession of the disputed property was taken over by the Government Accommodation Directorate, Ministry of Works and the Ministry of Works let out the same to the National Security Intelligence Department (NSI) on 27.08.1976. In such circumstances, the writ petitioner-respondents filed the instant writ petition and obtained Rule. 

 6. The appellants of Civil Appeal No.191 of 2015, who are the respondents of the Civil Review Petition No.334 of 2019, have-preferred that appeal upon getting leave against the judgment and decree dated 11.03.2012 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.157 of 2001 affirming those dated 18.06.2000 passed by the then learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.232 of 1997. The Government filed the said suit for declaration of its title and recovery of khas possession stating, inter alia, that the Government represented by the Collector, Dhaka, being owner of the disputed property, leased out the same to Professor Satyendra Nath Roy by a registered lease deed dated 08.12.1937 which became effective on and from 01.01.1938. It was alleged that violating the terms of the said lease deed, Professor Roy transferred the disputed property to his wife Sujata Roy by a registered deed of gift dated 18.05.1940. Subsequently, Sujata Roy sold the same to Munshi Ashraf Ali, father of the defendants 1-3, by a registered kabala dated 26.03.1951. Thereafter, Munshi Ashraf Ali got the period of lease extended by another registered lease deed dated 07.08.1961 with effect from 01.04.1961 to 31.03.1991. During continuance of the period of lease, the Government took over possession of the disputed property on 17.69.1971 in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 for the purpose of construction of the building of National Press Club. Subsequently when the Press Club was given alternative land, the disputed property was handed over to the Government Accommodation Directorate. In the meantime, period of lease of Munshi Ashraf Ali had expired on 31.03.1991 but his heirs did not apply for further renewal of the periodical lease and the lessor-Government automatically became owner of the disputed property on 31.03.1991. However, the heirs of Ashraf Ali started claiming the right, title to and possession in the same from 07.03.1993. They filed Writ Petition No.333 of 1993 challenging the act of taking over possession by the Government in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70, which gave rise to the cause or action for filing the suit by the Government for declaration of title to and recovery of khan possession in the suit property with further declaration that the defendants 1-3 have no right, title to and interest in the disputed property. 

 12. The disputed property is measuring an area of .4927 acre = 1(one) bigha 9 (nine) kathas 13 chattacks of Khas Mahal plot No.188, Sheet No.20 Ward No. 3, Municipal Holing no.14/1, Topkhana Road, Touzi No.15725. It was recorded in C.S. plot No.53 to the extent of .06 acre and C.S. plot No. 55 to the extent of .42 acre under C.S. khatian No.6947/6947(A) and R.S. plot No. 544 under R.S. khatian No.2089.
